entry.dc:title: Sediment control for the surface mining industry.
entry.dc:creator: Lagasse P.F.
entry.dc:description: The paper presents a discussion of the physical processes of erosion and sedimentation in relation to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and Office of Surface Mining regulations for sediment control in effluent from surface coal mines. The processes of erosion and sedimentation were studied extensively, and although quite complex, they may be characterized by modern simulation techniques to predict sediment loads from disturbed and undisturbed lands. Therefore, it is possible to design systems to control sediment from coal mining activities using such techniques as are discussed in the paper. The authors, however, contend that one cannot treat sediment uniformly as a pollutant and, at the same time, minimize disturbances to the hydrologic balance. (from authors' abstract)

entry.dc:title: Sedimentation in the East Branch Mahoning Creek basin, Clearfield and Jefferson Counties, Pennsylvania, June 1979 to June 1980.
entry.dc:creator: Wetzel K.
entry.dc:description: Parts of the basin, a forested area of 29.6 square miles in west-central Pennsylvania, are disturbed by farming, surface mining, unpaved haul roads, eroding reclaimed areas, and logging. Streamflow was measured and water samples collected at a site upstream from the mouth during base flow and storm periods to evaluate sediment discharges. An additional site on a tributary draining mostly farmland was also sampled. Samples were analyzed for suspended sediment, turbidity, and specific conductance. Daily mean suspended-sediment concentrations and discharges were computed. From June 1979 to June 1980, 3570 tons of suspended sediment was transported from the basin. This was an average yield of 121 tons mi<sup>2</sup>/yr.-from US Govt Reports Announcements, 19, 1982

entry.dc:title: Proceedings of the conference on water and energy: technical and policy issues.
entry.dc:creator: Kilpatrick F.
entry.dc:description: Industrial, political, legal, hydrological, and environmental issues surrounding development of energy and associated water resources are examined. Water use and requirements, and wastewater treatment are examined in respect to the synthetic fuel industry, coal slurry pipelines, surface mining, hydropower, and oil shale production. Water conservation and reuse, trends in energy/water legislation, policy and public management, and citizen participation in energy/water resource problems are reviewed. Attention is given to new energy resources and impacts, and to water related research needs for energy development.-from ASCE Publications Abstracts

entry.dc:title: Instability of contoured surface- mined landscapes in the northern Great Plains: causes and implications.
entry.dc:creator: Groenewold G.
entry.dc:description: Reclamation of surface-mined landscapes is commonly defined only in terms of biological productivity. Other critical concerns associated with surface mining include the long-term quality of groundwater and the stability of the post-mining landscape. Types of instability include area-wide settling, localized collapse and piping.-from Authors

entry.dc:title: Seismicity induced by surface mining: the Belchatow, Poland, earthquake of 29 November 1980.
entry.dc:creator: Gibowicz S.
entry.dc:description: On 29 November 1980 a magnitude 4.6 earthquake occurred in the brown coal mining area of Belchatow in central Poland. The tremor is characterized by a seismic moment M<inf>o</inf> = 2.5 X 10<sup>22</sup> dyne-cm, source radius r = 810m and stress drop DELTA sigma = 21 bar. The fault plane solution, found from P-wave first motion at 28 stations, is unfortunately not univocal and it implies either strike-slip fault motion with a left lateral transcurrent faulting or dip-slip motion with considerable strike-component on a reversed fault. The tremor was felt on large area and a maximum intensity was 7 of the MSK-64 scale. From the isoseismal map the depth was estimated to be approx 2km.-AuthorsInst of Geophys, Polish Acad of Sci, 00-973 Warsaw, PO Box 155, Pasteura 4, Poland.

entry.dc:title: Reproductive success of grassland sparrows on a reclaimed surface mine in West Virginia.
entry.dc:creator: Wray T.
entry.dc:description: Examines the reproductive success of grasshopper sparrows Ammodramus savannarum, savannah sparrows Passerculus sandwichensis, vesper sparrows Pooecetes gramineus and field sparrows Spizella pusilla. Only vesper sparrows showed significant annual differences in clutch size. Predation was the major cause of egg and nestling losses. The study site, surrounded by woodlots and pastureland, concentrated predators. Northern black racers Coluber constrictor constrictor and common crows Corvus brachyrhynchos were the major predators. Variable nesting success reflects differential predation pressure. Adults are not replacing themselves and immigration is necessary to maintain a stable population. Environmental cues are sufficient to elicit a settling response, but, due to predation, reproductive success is low. Although surface mining is providing new nesting habitat, inadequate reproductive success suggests that these man-made grasslands may not be of benefit to the sparrow populations. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: (The Belchatow earthquakes induced by surface mining, Central Poland)).
entry.dc:creator: Gibowicz S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Polish Academy of Sciences Publications Inst Geophysics Series M
entry.dc:description: Five seismic events which occurred between August 1979 and May 1980 in the Belchatow trench area in Central Poland, where large brown coal deposits are situated and where surface mining works have been carried out since 1976, are described. The three largest shocks are characterized by the local magnitude M<inf>L</inf> = 3.5, seismic moment M<inf>o</inf> = 7.5X10<sup>13</sup> N.m and source radius r = 350 m, approximately. The tremors were felt with maximum intensity between 5 and 6, and from the magnitude-intensity-depth relation the focus depth was tentatively estimated to be between 1 and 5 km. The Belchatow tremors are the manifestation of an unusual type of induced seismicity - seismicity connected with surface mining. The removal of the overburden and drainage of coal deposits by extensive ground water withdrawal seem to be direct factors responsible for stress concentration, though the preexisting tectonic stress might well be the most important indirect factor responsible for the origin of these events.-English summary

entry.dc:title: Some chemical characteristics of mine drainage in Illinois.
entry.dc:creator: Toler L.
entry.prism:publicationName: US Geological Survey Water Supply Paper
entry.dc:description: Surface mining for coal in Illinois has affected runoff from the mined areas and altered water quality in the streams. Average annual sulfate loads in streams are 3000-4000 tons per square mile of mined land in the Big Muddy and Saline River basins in S Illinois. Relatively high concentrations of dissolved aluminum, arsenic, chromium, copper, iron, manganese, and zinc are commonly associated with concentrations of sulfate greater than about 2000 milligrams per liter.-Author

entry.dc:title: Remote sensing applications to the Pennsylvania abandoned mine reclamation program.
entry.dc:creator: Clemens E.
entry.prism:publicationName: Proc National Conference on Energy Resource Management Baltimore 1982 Vol 2
entry.dc:description: Pennsylvania Abandoned Mine Land Inventory demonstrated the effective use of remote sensing techniques within the context of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977. The inventory combined data from field work, a literature search, and photointerpretation. A primary project objective was to identify accurately and map all surface features and disturbances from abandoned surface and underground mining. Black-and-white aerial photographs were used to record pits, contour benches, highwalls, spoil material, graded and recontoured areas, impounded water, and serious erosion and slide prone areas. In addition, vegetation cover estimates and surrounding land uses were noted. -from STAR, 21(15) , 1983

entry.dc:title: Reclamation planning in California - a cooperative approach ( mining).
entry.dc:creator: Mankoski Z.
entry.dc:description: An overview of the way in which the issue of mining land reclamation has been handled in the US since the early 1970s. Mining is seen increasingly as an interim land use, reflected in planning applications and the Surface Mining and Reclamation Act (SMARA) of 1975. Increasing public awareness of the importance of resource management is a goal of the CDMG Reclamation Program.-after Author

entry.dc:title: Nematode densities on reclaimed sites on a cold desert shrub- steppe.
entry.dc:creator: Stanton N.
entry.dc:description: Nematode populations were sampled under shrubs (Atriplex confertifolia), grasses and an introduced annual (Halogeton glomeratus) in a cold desert native shrub-steppe and on 3 neighboring sites disturbed by topsoil removal or surface mining. Of these 4 treatments, the native vegetation consistently supported the highest densities of all trophic groups of nematodes. On all sites, the native shrub, A. confertifolia, supported the highest densities while the introduced annual, H. glomeratus, supported the lowest.-from Authors

entry.dc:title: Ohio's abandoned mine lands reclamation program: a study of data collection and evaluation techniques.
entry.dc:creator: Sperry S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Proc National Conference on Energy Resource Management Baltimore 1982 Vol 2 Applications
entry.dc:description: The planning process for a statewide reclamation plan of Ohio abandoned minelands in response to the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 included: 1) the development of a screening and ranking methodology; 2) the establishment of a statewide review of major watersheds affected by mining; 3) the development of an immediate action process; and 4) a prototypical study of a priority watershed demonstrating the data collection, analysis, display and evaluation to be used for the remaining state watersheds.-from STAR, 21(15), 1983

entry.dc:title: UNIQUE METHOD TO ENRICH MINE SPOILS.
entry.dc:creator: Younos T.
entry.dc:description: The paper reviews studies which show that rice cultivation on sludge-amended mine spoils offers sound practice to retain runoff water and build up fertility during reclamation phase of surface mining.

entry.dc:title: DETERMINING THE OPTIMAL DEPTH OF AN OPEN PIT.
entry.dc:creator: Nilsson D.
entry.dc:description: To determine the optimal depth of an open pit, the Office of Surface Mining, US Department of the Interior, is sponsoring a research project at Michigan Technological University titled ″The effects of increasing energy costs on the future relation between open-pit and underground mining.″ This article analyzes the economic value of various pit depths for one hypothetical example from the project. The conclusion is that with a price of 5/ton of ore, the deposit can be mined with open pit methods down to a depth of 200 m, with future underground mining being unprofitable. With a price of 10/ton, open-pit mining can proceed down to a depth of 300 m. It would be more profitable, however, to change over to underground mining at 250 m depth.

entry.dc:title: Watersheds in muskeg terrain. 2. Evaluations based on water chemistry
entry.dc:creator: Schwartz F.W.
entry.dc:description: This paper discusses the application of data on stream water chemistry to regional groundwater evaluation, hydrograph separation, and evaluation of the effects of basin disturbance. We have selected for analysis the Firebag, Steepbank and Muskeg River basins, and Hartley and Thickwood Creek basins in northern Alberta, Canada. They cover slightly more than 9000 km<sup>2</sup> within a region containing vast quantities of surface mineable, oil sand deposits. All basins are drift covered and underlain by bedrock that can range in age from Precambrian to Cretaceous. Comparison of chemical data for stream water from all basins with that for groundwater from Hartley Creek basin confirms that groundwater is a major source of streamflow in winter. Indications are that this groundwater inflow is almost entirely from glacial drift. Hydrograph separations based on chemical parameters indicate that during the spring and summer the proportion of groundwater in the streamflow is less than winter values with the largest contribution by far coming from the drainage of muskeg. Muskeg thus exerts important control on stream discharge and chemistry. If surface mining in these basins causes the removal of muskeg and replacement by mineral soil, stream discharge from affected areas will be less during summer and more during spring runoff and stormflow periods. As well, major-ion concentrations should be generally higher in the summer and fall months. However, the impact of local disturbances in a larger basin will be diminished downstream as waters from affected areas are mixed with other waters. © 1982.

entry.dc:title: IMPACT OF PUBLIC POLICY ON SURFACE MINE PLANNING AND DESIGN IN THE UNITED STATES.
entry.dc:creator: Sweigard R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The major effects that public policy has had on the planning design, and organization of surface mines in the United States are summarized in this paper. The public policy impacts are grouped into three separate categories: mine planning, mine design, and mine organization. A clear distinction is made between the Federal, state, and local governmental responsibilities in formulating public policy with regard to surface mining operations.

entry.dc:title: STATUS OF TECHNOLOGY IN SURFACE MINING IN INDIA.
entry.dc:creator: Mozumdar B.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: In this article, the status of Indian surface mining activity in different mineral sectors are first reviewed followed by some observations of general interest. It is shown that surface mining is destined to play a pivotal role in meeting the mineral and fuel need of the country. The expertise available within the country as well as the expanding machine manufacturing capability will help in sustaining its pace of rapid development. Adequate mandatory steps will be necessary in ensuring environmental protection.

entry.dc:title: ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT OF SURFACE COAL MINING IN THE UNITED STATES.
entry.dc:creator: Chugh Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Surface coal mining contributes over 60% of the U. S. coal production. Environmental constraints on surface coal mining have been increasing for the past two decades and have resulted in a substantial decline in productivity. This paper briefly describes the different acts and agencies regulating surface mining, primary mining and reclamation techniques, overall environmental assessment, regional environment concerns and their abatement.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING TECHNIQUES - A GLOBAL REVIEW.
entry.dc:creator: Rickus J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: Surface mining methods in use world-wide for the extraction of stratified and metalliferous minerals are briefly examined, together with the equipment for excavation, loading and transportation. Trends in the development of mining equipment, their application, and mine planning techniques are discussed. Some of the important mine developments throughout the world are reviewed.

entry.dc:title: SURFACE MINING - PAST, PRESENT AND FUTURE.
entry.dc:creator: Atkinson T.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The article reviews the history, current state-of-the-art and future trends of development in the field of surface mining. The main topics discussed cover the limits of scale of surface mining operations performed by walking draglines and bucket wheel excavators; mine design and planning for strip, terrace and open-pit mining; ground preparation including drilling and blasting operations; loading and haulage equipment; and surface mine electric power systems.

entry.dc:title: FOURTH ANNUAL DIRECTORY OF NEW TECHNOLOGY.
